# Instrument types

Add an instrument from the [Orchestra](orchestra.qmd) Arrangement, give it
an ID, then create Score notes that target that ID. Use **Project → Generate
CSD to Screen** to see the resulting `instr` block. A project's instrument
can also have Global Orchestra, Global Score, and embedded UDO code; these
travel with the instrument when copied between projects.

## Generic Instrument

Use **Generic Instrument** when you already have Csound orchestra text.
Enter the instrument _body_ in its **Instrument** tab; Blue creates the
surrounding `instr <ID>` and `endin`. The **UDO** tab stores local opcode
definitions. **Global Orc** and **Global Sco** hold supporting statements
emitted outside the instrument. For example, `blueMixerOut` can route the
instrument through Blue's [Mixer](mixer.qmd).

## BlueSynthBuilder

**BlueSynthBuilder** combines Csound code with a graphical control
interface. In **Interface**, turn on **Edit Mode** to add and arrange
widgets, set their object names and ranges, and configure the grid. Turn
Edit Mode off to use the controls. A widget named `amplitude` can supply
the replacement key `<amplitude>` in Csound code. Blue substitutes its
current value or generated automation signal when building the CSD.

The **Code** tab has four parts: **Instrument** for per-note Csound code,
**Always On** for an associated continuously running instrument, and
**Global Orc** and **Global Sco** for supporting statements. The **UDO**
tab keeps dependent opcodes with the instrument. To share a self-contained
instrument, include required UDOs there and use its global sections for
shared setup; inspect the generated CSD for duplicate tables or names.

Use the interface's **Presets** menu to save or recall widget values.
Presets save values, not widget layout. Supported widgets can expose
[Parameter automation](parameter-automation.qmd); write their replacement
keys where a Csound control-rate signal is legal. To expose a supported
control, select its widget in Edit Mode and enable **Automation** in
Properties. For an always-on audio
chain, the main code can send through `blueMixerOut` and the always-on code
can read with `blueMixerIn` before routing onward. This requires the mixer
to be enabled. Start with a simple instrument and verify its output before
adding more routing.

## BlueX7

**BlueX7** is Blue's six-operator FM instrument. Its current editor has
**Voice & Global**, **Operators**, **Pitch Envelope**, and **Csound** tabs.
The first tab contains common voice settings, LFO controls, and an
algorithm chooser. The Operators tab edits one of six operators; the
Pitch Envelope tab edits the shared pitch contour. The Csound tab is for
additional Csound processing and output routing.

**Import SysEx…** loads a DX7 voice or lets you choose one from a bank.
Confirm the selected voice before it replaces the current settings.
The editor offers local undo and redo for voice edits. Test a short
[GenericScore](generic-score.qmd) event against its Arrangement ID. As in
the older BlueX7 score convention, `p4` supplies pitch and `p5` velocity;
check the generated CSD and resulting sound after importing a legacy bank.

## Python Instrument

The **Python Instrument** editor stores Jython code that generates a
Csound instrument body. Its **Test** button evaluates the code and shows
the generated text or an error. Rendering requires the Java runtime
session; if that service is unavailable, code generation fails. The
editor also contains embedded UDO and global code tabs. Test the
generated instrument before relying on an older Python project.

## JavaScript Instrument

**JavaScript Instrument** evaluates its script and uses the resulting
`instrument` string as the Csound orchestra body. For example:

```javascript
instrument = 'aTone oscili p4, p5\nouts aTone, aTone';
```

Its UDO and global code tabs remain available. Blue 3 runs the script with
its embedded JavaScript runtime during CSD generation; inspect **Project →
Generate CSD to Screen** to confirm the generated body and resolve any
script error before rendering. Scripts that depend on the older Java
application's host APIs may need revision.
